// 01 — About

Who I Am

I'm a Mechanical Engineering master's student at Southern University and a Graduate Research Assistant. My research uses machine learning and graph neural networks to predict material behavior. I've gotten good at Python, PyTorch, and solving hard technical problems.

But here's the honest truth. My real passion is robotics.

Over the past year, I've been shifting everything toward robotics and autonomous systems. I am combining my mechanical engineering background with machine learning, control, and robotics software. I am not waiting to feel ready. I am actively building.

What excites me is building systems that intelligently interact with the physical world. I want to build robots that work in messy real world environments, not just in clean simulations. That combination of intelligence and physical engineering means a lot to me.

I have been learning ROS2, Linux robotics workflows, simulations, and system integration on my own. I have done mechatronics projects with servo motors, PWM control, manipulators, and microcontrollers. I genuinely enjoy learning this stuff even when it is hard.

I currently have a 4.0 GPA while balancing research, coursework, and robotics self study. But I care more about actually understanding things than just getting grades. I dig into fundamentals until things make sense.

I have also done engineering internships in large scale industrial environments. Being around real fabrication yards and construction workflows taught me discipline and adaptability. It made me sure that I want to build systems that solve real problems.

One thing about me is that I go the extra mile when I care. If I have a gap, I close it on my own. I do not wait for opportunities to prepare me. I prepare myself first. That is why I am serious about robotics.

I have been talking with professors about a possible PhD in robotics and adaptive control. But right now, what I really want is hands on industry experience through an internship. I have the foundation. I am hungry to be in a place where robots are actually built and deployed.

I want to learn from experienced engineers and contribute through hard work and curiosity. I enjoy difficult challenges and collaborative teams. My goal is to become the kind of engineer who builds intelligent systems that actually function in the real world. That is what I am working toward every day.

// 06 — Research

Current Work

// Active Research — NSF Funded
ML for Thermomechanical Property Prediction of Polymer Materials

Developing machine learning models — including Artificial Neural Networks and Graph Convolutional Networks — to predict the thermomechanical behavior of polymer systems. Using molecular graph representations and physics-informed modeling to improve prediction accuracy. Validates model outputs against experimental DMA datasets for physical consistency. Part of an NSF-funded initiative on AI-enabled materials design at Southern University.

// Paper In Progress — Robotics · Multi-Agent RL
Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Safe Collaborative Assembly in Human-Robot Shared Workspaces

A Two-Stage Framework Using Behavioural Cloning and MADDPG Coordination

Addresses a critical gap in multi-agent deep RL: deploying multiple collaborative robots safely alongside human workers in shared assembly environments. Most existing MARL research operates in agent-only simulations — human presence is rarely modelled, and safe RL is largely limited to single-agent settings.
